tagline: Reboot without losing your Claude Code sessions in Warp.
summary: Warp does not bring back the agents that ran in it. warp-session-restore remembers every Claude Code session running on the machine, and after a reboot reopens each one in Warp, grouped by the folder it runs in, resumed where it was.
capabilities: Snapshots every running Claude Code CLI session on each session start and turn end: its folder, name and the launch flags worth replaying (remote control, permission mode, model, effort, extra dirs)
Groups sessions by folder: the git repository they run in, worktrees and subfolders included, else the folder itself
Restores each session in a Warp tab running claude --resume in place: same session id, same Remote Control entry
Resumes a session its repository's launcher started through that launcher, and a detached session detached again
Drops a session closed with /exit from the snapshot, keeps one a shutdown stopped
Opens them in the window of the Warp already running, or starts Warp with one colored tab group per folder
Waits until every resumed session runs again, and says which did not
Restores only the sessions you name, or previews with --dry-run
Checks that Warp's Claude Code plugin (agent notifications) is enabled
